Independent code computes angular unions and area quadrature for four shapes, and a separate direct 75,000-sample Haar-pair metric Monte Carlo checks predicted CDF values. originality.rationale: A scalar distribution inverse theorem is proved by newly recovering the unordered strict Voronoi-facet distance multiset from square-root changes in the derivative of the Haar two-point geodesic-distance law. Available literature explains cut-locus Hessians, planar lattice classification using different data (lattice neighbour sequences), and directional Fourier signatures of the full distance kernel, none of which supplies the scalar-histogram-to-facet inversion. Multiple targeted actual searches found no directly covering theorem; residual discovery risk is recorded.
residual_risks: A historical exact formula for radial distance distributions of lattice Voronoi cells may already implicitly yield the same inverse theorem, including multiplicities; searches cannot rule out inaccessible/nonindexed work.
The distinction from nearby data-completeness literature depends on the scalar histogram carrying no direction or lattice-site labels; no publication-priority guarantee is asserted.

value.rationale: Answers a natural complete inverse metric-measure question for all flat two-tori: an unlabeled pair-distance histogram is complete for Euclidean isometry despite having discarded spatial directions. The exact singular multiplicities and constructive Gram recovery illuminate the geometry of cut loci and nontrivial rectangular/hexagonal transition, beyond known single moments, neighbor-distance data, and a routine special-case computation.
